final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 forms the internal aldimine with the PLP cofactor; removing its side chain should abolish catalysis while leaving the fold largely intact.
Arg preserves positive charge but cannot form the correct PLP aldimine, so catalytic activity is likely lost; slightly riskier than Ala due to possible partial cofactor coordination.
Proline substitution at a conserved glycine rigidifies the backbone and can strongly destabilize the fold, plausibly abolishing activity through structural disruption.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence available and the catalytic-lysine hypothesis is strong enough that additional LLM-only rounds add little value.

history.rationale: K119 is the catalytic PLP Schiff-base lysine in human CBS; substitution to Ala eliminates the internal aldimine and abolishes catalysis.
K119 is the catalytic PLP Schiff-base lysine (conserved TSGNTG motif region); removing the side chain that forms the internal aldimine should abolish activity. Kept top.
Arg preserves charge but cannot form the essential PLP Schiff base at the reactive position, blocking cofactor-based catalysis.
Arg preserves positive charge but cannot form the correct PLP aldimine geometry; likely LOF but slightly riskier than Ala since bulky Arg may still partially coordinate. Slightly reduced.
T257 (part of the highly conserved TSGN PLP-binding/glycine-rich loop) contributes to cofactor and substrate positioning; disruption likely severely impairs activity.
Ala substitution at a possible active-site/interface residue; plausible but weaker mechanistic basis than the catalytic lysine.
This conserved Asn in the substrate-binding region contacts substrate/cofactor; Ala substitution should reduce catalytic competence.
N149 near PLP-binding region could disrupt cofactor coordination; moderate confidence LOF.
Glycine in the conserved TSGNTG cofactor loop provides backbone flexibility; a rigid proline disrupts the PLP-binding loop conformation and likely inactivates the enzyme.
GTGGT motif glycine; Pro likely disrupts the glycine-rich loop but structural criticality less certain than G307.
Conserved active-site arginine implicated in substrate carboxylate binding; charge reversal should disrupt substrate recognition and catalysis.
Charge reversal may disrupt local interactions but surface Arg substitutions often tolerated; kept as lower-tier.
Glycine in a conserved GTGG active-site motif provides flexibility; proline substitution should perturb the catalytic loop and reduce activity.
Gly-to-Pro backbone rigidification at a conserved glycine can strongly destabilize the fold and abolish activity; promoted above other Gly/Thr-to-Pro candidates.
Introducing proline near the conserved PLP-binding loop is likely to distort catalytic geometry and impair cofactor function.
Redundant with the stronger G259P/G307P Pro-insertion hypotheses and weaker mechanistic rationale; dropped to focus the pool.
